## Intro

This edition covers the week of 23-29 November 2026 and reports developments for commercial road freight in Poland, with priority for heavy, oversize and special transport. Reports: Poland extends daily driving time for domestic LPG tanker drivers until 6 December.

This edition was prepared after its scheduled release on 2026-11-20T11:00:00.000Z. It covers 2026-W48; the publication date above records the delayed release.

## Lead reports

### Poland extends daily driving time for domestic LPG tanker drivers until 6 December

According to an industry report, the Polish Minister of Infrastructure has introduced a further temporary derogation from EU rules on driving time, breaks and rest periods for drivers carrying LPG (liquefied petroleum gas). Drivers on these journeys may drive up to 11 hours per day. The report says an earlier similar derogation was issued in March for fuel tanker drivers.

**Category:** Operational development  
**Where:** Poland, national road transport only. The report states the derogation covers domestic LPG carriage.  
**Affected vehicles:** Goods vehicles carrying LPG in tanks on domestic journeys in Poland, with drivers subject to EU driving and rest time rules (tachograph-using vehicles). The excerpt does not give a weight threshold.  
**When:** 6 November 2026 to 6 December 2026

**Impact:** Domestic LPG tanker operations in Poland have more scheduling flexibility, with up to 11 hours of daily driving. Cross-border journeys are not covered according to the report, so the standard EU rules continue to apply there. The report also notes that more flexibility for carriers does not necessarily benefit drivers. Break and rest provisions beyond the 11-hour figure are not stated in the available excerpt.

**Recommended action:** Obtain the official ministerial notice and check the exact conditions (daily limit, breaks, rest, records and documents to carry) before using the derogation. Do not apply it to international journeys or to non-LPG loads. Make sure tachograph records and driver briefings reflect the derogation. Plan a return to standard EU limits after 6 December 2026.

**Exemptions/conditions:** This is itself a derogation from EU driving-time rules. It applies only to domestic LPG carriage per the report. No wider exemption is confirmed. The report does not address oversize or abnormal transport.

*Source: [e-truckbus.pl](https://e-truckbus.pl/czas-jazdy-kierowcow-cystern-lpg-11-godzin/) — Industry report — not an official authority notice*
